one_month_reasoning: Three scheduled events fall in the window. (1) TSMC's September sales come out on Oct 8 and its Q3 call is on Oct 15 (src 30). August revenue was a record, +53% y/y, and N2 has 4x the tape-outs of N3 (src 28, 29), so I expect a positive read for design demand. (2) Cadence reports Q3 on 2026-10-26, now confirmed (src 35). The guide is revenue of $1.595-1.625B and EPS of $2.01-2.07. Backlog is a record $8.1B, of which $4.2B is current (src 1, 22). The peer read is strong: Synopsys raised FY26 and guided FY27 to +15% (src 3, 4), and Siemens EDA grew more than 30% (src 18). So a beat-and-raise is the most likely outcome, but the market largely expects one. (3) The stock has already run about 24% from the week of 9/14 (close $282.90) to $350.75, including +6.2% on 10/1 in sympathy with the Synopsys investor day (src 20, 37). After a move that fast, short-term reversal risk roughly offsets post-earnings drift and momentum. A headline about AI-disruption (Kimi-type demos, src 5) can return at any time. Net: the median is roughly at spot (~$351.5) with about 12.5% one-month vol (the usual 41%/3.5 = 11.7%, plus a bit for the earnings event), and the spread is symmetric. The 1-month ladder is unchanged from my capped run because nothing found changes the event calendar or the balance of short-horizon risks.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (75%): NTM non-GAAP EPS at the horizon of about $11.0 (between FY27 consensus $9.76 and FY28 consensus $11.39) x 34x = $374, and FCF yield (25%): FY28E FCF $2.55B at a 3.1% yield less about $1.0B net debt over 275M shares = $296. Blended $355.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM (Q4'27-Q3'28) non-GAAP EPS ~$11.0 x 34x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: 0.25 x FY27 run-rate plus 0.75 x FY28. Consensus is $9.76 and $11.39, which gives about $11.0. I don't haircut it: the industry chain supports about 15-17% EPS growth. Synopsys guides mid-teens revenue and mid-20s EPS CAGR (src 3), Siemens EDA is growing more than 30% (src 18), and Cadence's backlog is up 27% (src 22).

Today the stock is at about 36x FY27 consensus ($350.73/$9.76). Its 5-year average forward P/E is about 44x (src 34). Synopsys trades at about 25x its FY27 non-GAAP EPS guide ($475.70/$19.08, src 20, 3), though it carries lower margins and Ansys integration. I use 34x: below Cadence's own history to price the AI-agent commoditisation overhang, and keeping a premium to Synopsys for margin (45.5% vs ~44%) and execution.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28E FCF $2.55B / 3.1% = EV $82.3B; less net debt ~$1.0B; / 275M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: $2.48B notes less $1.44B cash, held roughly flat: FCF covers buybacks (remaining authorisation $1.0B, src 16) and the 2027 maturity is refinanced or repaid.
275.4M outstanding at 6/30/2026 (src 16). Buybacks offset SBC and the 3.2M Hexagon shares already issued (src 38).
FY26 FCF ~$1.85B (OCF $2.0B less ~$0.15B capex, src 1), grown ~17-18%/yr. That is below Synopsys' mid-20s FCF CAGR target (src 3) and in line with consensus EPS growth (src 17).

Synopsys' FY27 FCF guide of ~$3.1B (src 3) against its market value after the 10/1 move (src 20) implies roughly a 3.5% yield. Cadence has historically traded at a premium to Synopsys, so I apply 3.1%.

bear.story: Agentic and open-source AI flows (Kimi K3, well-funded startups like ChipAgents, Cognichip and Ricursive) start pressuring seat pricing at mature nodes, and the story spreads. Or the hyperscaler capex debate (only one of six forecast FCF-positive in 2027) triggers a design-spend pause that hits lumpy hardware and IP. EPS still reaches about $10.5-11, but the multiple compresses to about 23-24x, near where Synopsys trades.

base.story: The industry keeps compounding at mid-teens: Synopsys FY27 +15%, EDA 13%+ long-term, Siemens EDA >30%, ESDA +12.7%, TSMC N2 tape-outs 4x N3. Cadence delivers roughly consensus ($9.76 FY27, $11.39 FY28). The multiple holds at about 34x as agentic-AI monetisation (subscription plus consumption) shows up as accretive rather than cannibalising.

bull.story: Custom silicon (Broadcom's and Marvell's expanding XPU rosters) and $1.3T of 2027 hyperscaler capex drive record hardware, IP and SD&A. Cadence's agent pricing ('worth tens of thousands of dollars' per virtual engineer) starts adding visibly to growth, the way GPT-Synopsys did for Synopsys' multiple. EPS of about $11.5 re-rates toward the 5-year average forward P/E (~42-44x).

thesis_break_reason: $255 is below both the 52-week low ($262.75, set 2026-02-03) and the September 2026 panic low (~$273). On ~$11 NTM EPS it implies about 23x, Synopsys' multiple, despite Cadence's higher margins and record backlog. Getting there would most likely need fundamental damage: decelerating bookings or backlog, Synopsys or Siemens flagging price pressure, or real commercial adoption of agentic/open-source flows at advanced nodes (which today lack advanced PDK access). A sentiment swing alone probably wouldn't do it.

reasoning: This continuation re-ran about 30 searches and fetches, mostly in the industry lane, to verify the round-1 numbers that rested on thin sourcing. Confirmed: Synopsys' FY27 guide is $11.10-11.20B revenue, $19.04-19.12 EPS and ~$3.1B FCF, with an FY26-30 model of mid-teens revenue, EDA 13%+, IP 17%+, ~50% margin and mid-20s EPS/FCF CAGR, plus GPT-Synopsys (revenue share tied to measured PPA gains) and an AWS deal over $1B (src 3, 20, 21). Siemens EDA grew more than 30% in FQ3, with DI software +15%, but guided Q4 orders flat on tough EDA booking comps (src 18, 19). TSMC August revenue was +53% y/y and N2 tape-outs are 4x N3 (src 28, 29). FY28 consensus EPS of $11.39 now has a source (src 17) and supports my earlier $11.2 estimate. Corrections: the 52-week low of $262.75 was set on Feb 3, 2026, not in September; the September low was ~$273 (src 37). China risk is lower than I assumed, since the May 2025 licence regime was revoked in July 2025 (src 26), though China was ~15% of Q2 revenue (src 27). New bear evidence: Synopsys trades at only ~25x FY27 after its +9% day, which caps the premium Cadence can claim. AI-EDA startups have raised heavily: ChipAgents $134M, Cognichip $93M, Ricursive $300M (src 24, 25). Hyperscaler FCF is thin into $1.3T of 2027 capex (src 31). New bull evidence: Cadence prices agents as virtual engineers on subscription plus consumption (src 23). Advanced-PDK access remains the moat that open-source flows lack (src 6, 33). The consensus PT is ~$404-405 (src 11, 35). Valuation: P/E $374 (NTM $11.0 x 34x) x 0.75 plus FCF yield $296 x 0.25 gives $355. That is slightly below my capped-run $362, because I value on NTM rather than FY28 EPS and the Synopsys peer check lowers the FCF-yield value. The ladder is a mixture: 90% lognormal (median $365, sigma 0.31) plus 10% bear-tail lognormal (median $255, sigma 0.35), for an overall median of about $353. Sigma sits below the 41% realized vol because that was inflated by a one-off narrative shock, and the tail adds back disruption risk.
